matched_nodes.title: Transience implies ballisticity for uniformly elliptic i.i.d. RWRE (open, d >= 2) is a statement about the first moment of the regeneration time, and the polynomial condition (P)_M is a moment self-improvement
matched_nodes.body_excerpt:
PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Under (IID)+(UE) transience in direction l gives the Sznitman-Zerner regeneration structure with tau_1 < infinity a.s.; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 2.20). Under (UE) a trap of diameter r holds the walk at most exponentially long in r, so sub-ballistic behaviour needs polynomially rare traps of logarithmic size along the path, which i.i.d. environments do allow; the question is whether the tail P(tau_1 > n) can be as heavy as n^{-1+eps}. Open Question 3.20 (does positive velocity imply (P)_M for M > 15d + 5) is then the question whether a finite first moment of tau_1 self-improves to moments of order about M/d, because (P)_M is equivalent through the slab decomposition to high moments of tau_1. The Guerra-Ramirez theorem (T) <=> (T') (2018) settles Open Question 3.28 but neither of these. Recorded as the moment-self-improvement reformulation.
Random walk in i.i.d. uniformly elliptic environment on Z^d, d >= 2
Regeneration structure of Sznitman-Zerner

matched_nodes.title: Open problem: Transience in a direction implies ballisticity for uniformly elliptic i.i.d. RWRE in d >= 2
matched_nodes.body_excerpt:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status no_resolution_found_in_documented_search; result status attempted_unsolved). Let d >= 2 and the RWRE satisfy (UE) and (IID) and be transient in direction l. Is the walk necessarily ballistic in direction l? Source: Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment, Open question 2.20, p. 24. Status notes: Bounded search 2026-09-07: Guerra and Ramirez (arXiv 1809.02011, 'A proof of Sznitman's conjecture about ballistic RWRE') proved the equivalence of conditions (T) and (T'), which is Open question 3.28 of the source, NOT this question; no proof that transience implies ballisticity in d >= 2 was found.
